title: Art Timeline
headline: Are you an Art connoisseur?
tagline: One timeline and a few art movements.
intro: I've often found it challenging to easily understand the different art movements.
Which came first? Who are the key artists? What are their main works?
This quiz is my own attempt to remember these. I hope it will be useful for your own artistic explorations too.

verdicts.low: A first gallery visit — wander the timeline a little longer.
verdicts.mid: A developing eye — the outlines are there.
verdicts.high: A trained eye — the collection is in good hands.

questions.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.fact: The Mona Lisa is a Renaissance work — a period defined by realism, proportion, and mastery of perspective.

questions.prompt: The Starry Night belongs to which movement?
questions.fact: Van Gogh's The Starry Night is Post-Impressionist — a reaction against Impressionism (1880 – 1900).

questions.statement: The Renaissance was a period of renewed interest in classical art and humanism.
questions.fact: Renaissance art (1400 – 1600) revived classical ideals through realism, proportion, and perspective.

questions.prompt: Which movement chased the fleeting effects of light outdoors?
questions.fact: Impressionism (1860 – 1880): broken brushwork, vibrant colors, and a focus on the open air.

questions.prompt: Tap these movements in order, earliest first.
questions.fact: Renaissance (1400 – 1600), then Baroque (1600 – 1700), then Impressionism (1860 – 1880).

questions.prompt: Andy Warhol's Campbell's Soup I is an icon of which movement?
questions.fact: Pop Art (1950 – 1960) embraced mass-media imagery and consumer culture, often with a sense of humor.

questions.statement: Surrealism explored the unconscious mind and the realm of dreams.
questions.fact: Surrealism (1920 – 1940) leaned on illogical juxtapositions and dreamlike imagery.

questions.prompt: Girl with Balloon is a work by which artist?
questions.fact: Street Art (1980 – Today) grew out of graffiti, with deep roots in urban culture.

questions.prompt: Which of these movements appears earliest on the timeline?
questions.fact: Romanesque art (1000 – 1200): rounded arches, thick walls, and religious subject matter.

questions.prompt: Who painted The Kiss?
questions.fact: Klimt's The Kiss belongs to Art Nouveau (1890 – 1910), with its organic shapes and stylized motifs.

questions.prompt: Neoclassicism arose as a reaction against the excesses of which movement?
questions.fact: Neoclassicism (1780 – 1830) answered Rococo with order, balance, and simplicity.

questions.prompt: Who painted Las Meninas?
questions.fact: Velázquez's Las Meninas is a Baroque work (1600 – 1700).

questions.prompt: Tap these movements in order, earliest first.
questions.fact: Rococo (1700 – 1780), Romanticism (1800 – 1850), then Realism (1840 – 1880).

questions.statement: Realism aimed to idealize its subjects.
questions.fact: Realism (1840 – 1880) portrayed the world as it is — everyday subjects, with idealism avoided.

questions.prompt: Chiaroscuro — dramatic light and shadow — defines which movement?
questions.fact: Baroque art (1600 – 1700) paired chiaroscuro with dramatic poses and emotional intensity.

questions.prompt: Jacques-Louis David's Oath of the Horatii belongs to which movement?
questions.fact: David painted all three Neoclassical works on this timeline, including Napoleon at the Great St. Bernard.

questions.prompt: Which movement fused art, craft, and technology into functional design?
questions.fact: The Bauhaus (1919 – 1938) put design at the center of daily life, free of unnecessary ornamentation.

questions.statement: On this timeline, Impressionism begins before Realism.
questions.fact: Realism starts in 1840; Impressionism follows in 1860.

questions.prompt: The Persistence of Memory is by which artist?
questions.fact: Dalí's melting clocks are Surrealism at its purest (1920 – 1940).

questions.prompt: Organic shapes, asymmetry, and stylized plant motifs define which movement?
questions.fact: Art Nouveau (1890 – 1910) is a decorative and flowing style.

levels.name: Connoisseur
levels.tagline: Exact dates and deep cuts, against the clock.

questions.prompt: In which year does Cubism begin on the timeline?
questions.fact: Cubism runs 1907 – 1914: multiple perspectives and fragmented geometric forms.

questions.prompt: The Port at Sunset, Opus 236 (Saint-Tropez) is by which artist?
questions.fact: Signac sits in Post-Impressionism (1880 – 1900), alongside Seurat's pointillism.

questions.prompt: Tap these movements in order, earliest first.
questions.fact: Cubism (1907), then Bauhaus (1919) — opening just one year before Surrealism (1920).

questions.statement: Kay Sage's Margin of Silence is a Surrealist work.
questions.fact: Sage hangs alongside Magritte and Dalí in Surrealism (1920 – 1940).

questions.prompt: Which movement's experiments spanned pointillism, fauvism, and expressionism?
questions.fact: Post-Impressionism (1880 – 1900) was less one style than a laboratory of styles.

questions.prompt: Who painted The Ninth Wave?
questions.fact: Aivazovsky's seascape carries Romanticism's love of drama and the sublime (1800 – 1850).

questions.prompt: Marcel Breuer's B5 chair belongs to which movement?
questions.fact: The B5 embodies the Bauhaus fusion of craft and industry (1919 – 1938).

questions.statement: Minimalism begins in the same year Pop Art ends.
questions.fact: Pop Art closes in 1960 exactly as Minimalism opens (1960 – 1970).

questions.prompt: Chris Burden's Urban Light appears under which movement?
questions.fact: Contemporary Art (1980 – Today) spans the breadth of today's globalized practice.

questions.prompt: What is the exact period of Neoclassicism?
questions.fact: Neoclassicism: 1780 – 1830, wedged between Rococo and Romanticism.

levels.tagline: Every trick in the collection, on a shorter clock.

questions.prompt: Which artist appears under both Realism and Impressionism on this timeline?
questions.fact: Manet hangs twice: The Old Musician in Realism, Luncheon on the Grass in Impressionism.

questions.statement: The Triumph of Venus is by Sandro Botticelli.
questions.fact: François Boucher painted The Triumph of Venus (Rococo); Botticelli's is The Birth of Venus.

questions.prompt: This embroidery belongs to which movement?
questions.fact: The Bayeux Tapestry opens the timeline with Romanesque (1000 – 1200).

questions.prompt: Tap these movements in order, earliest first.
questions.fact: A tight thirty years: Impressionism (1860), Post-Impressionism (1880), Art Nouveau (1890).

questions.prompt: Which movement's exact period is 1919 – 1938?
questions.fact: The Bauhaus school years bound the movement precisely: 1919 – 1938.

questions.prompt: Cindy Sherman's Untitled Film Still #21 appears under which movement?
questions.fact: Sherman's ironic self-staging belongs to Postmodernism (1965 – Today).

questions.statement: Exactly three movements on the timeline run to “Today”.
questions.fact: Four do: Conceptual Art, Postmodernism, Street Art, and Contemporary Art.

questions.prompt: Who made Mechanical Stage Design?
questions.fact: Schmidt's stage design sits in the Bauhaus alongside Breuer's B5 and Moholy-Nagy's Composition.

questions.prompt: This Manet canvas appears under which movement?
questions.fact: The Old Musician sits in Realism (1840 – 1880), before Manet's Impressionist entry.

questions.prompt: Rococo ends in 1780. Which movement begins that same year?
questions.fact: Neoclassicism (1780 – 1830) answers Rococo the year it closes.
